Templates, static files and blueprints

Source: vignettes/flask-flow.Rmd
flask-flow.Rmd

A small spigot app is a folder with app.R, a template or two and a www/ folder. Once an app has several sections, the files are easier to find in the layout a Flask developer would expect: templates in templates/, scripts and stylesheets in static/, and each section of the site in a blueprint that keeps its pages, endpoints, templates and files together. This vignette shows that layout. Every part of it is optional, and an app without it works as before.

The layout 

myapp/
├── app.R
├── api.R               # the app's own endpoints
├── R/
│   └── cars.R          # the cars blueprint
├── api/
│   └── cars.R          # the cars endpoints
├── templates/
│   ├── index.html
│   ├── partials/
│   │   └── nav.html
│   └── cars/
│       ├── list.html
│       └── model.html
└── static/
    ├── site.css
    └── cars/
        └── cars.js

app.R says where things are:

spigot_app(
  pages      = list("/" = spigot_page("index.html")),
  api        = "api.R",
  blueprints = list("/cars" = cars),
  templates  = "templates",
  partials   = "templates/partials",
  static     = "static"
)

templates is a search path. With it, spigot_page("index.html") names a template rather than a file next to app.R: spigot looks for templates/index.html, and only then for index.html in the app’s folder. It can list several folders, searched in order.

partials is a folder of partials every page can use, one per file: nav.html is {{> nav}}. A page’s own partials win over these, so one page can swap in its own nav.

static is a folder served at /static. Every page can load <link rel="stylesheet" href="static/site.css">, whatever its depth, because spigot gives nested pages a <base href> that points at the app’s root. httpuv serves these files directly, without running R. www/ keeps working alongside static/. Unlike www/, static/ is served however the app is launched (see Where paths start).

A blueprint

The cars section of the site is one blueprint, defined in R/cars.R:

cars <- spigot_blueprint(
  pages     = list("/" = spigot_page("list.html"), "/model" = spigot_page("model.html")),
  api       = "api/cars.R",
  templates = "templates/cars",
  partials  = "templates/cars/partials",
  static    = "static/cars"
)

spigot_app(blueprints = list("/cars" = cars)) mounts it at /cars:

  • Its pages are served under the prefix: / at /cars, /model at /cars/model. They are checked like the app’s own pages, so a path served twice is an error when the app is built.
  • Its endpoints are served under the app’s API, at /api/cars/..., behind the same session check. A page calls them with spigot.get("cars/fit").
  • Its templates are looked for in templates/cars/ first, then on the app’s search path, so the blueprint can override a shared template. Its partials win over the app’s, the same way.
  • Its static files are served at /cars/static, and each of its pages gets that path as {{static}}. The template does not need to know where the blueprint is mounted:
<script src="{{static}}/cars.js"></script>
# api/cars.R
#* @get /fit
function(x = "wt") {
  fit_cars(x)    # defined in R/, so available to the endpoints too
}

Blueprints live in R/ because Shiny loads every file there before it runs app.R, so cars exists by the time spigot_app() needs it, and functions defined in R/ are available to the endpoints. spigot adds no loader of its own. The Blueprints vignette covers them in full.

Compared with Flask

Flask spigot
Blueprint("cars", ...), url_prefix="/cars" spigot_blueprint(...), blueprints = list("/cars" = cars)
render_template("list.html") spigot_page("list.html")
url_for("cars.static", filename="cars.js") {{static}}/cars.js
a blueprint’s routes under /cars/... its endpoints under /api/cars/...
<int:id> in a route not yet: a page reads the query string with data = function(req)

whisker, spigot’s template engine, has no functions, so there is no url_for(). Relative URLs and {{static}} cover what it is used for.

Where paths start: root

Every path in spigot_app() and spigot_blueprint() (templates, partials, static folders, plumber files) is relative to root, and the files are read when spigot_app() builds the app. root defaults to the working directory at that moment. How the app is launched decides what that is (see “Running the app” in ?spigot_app):

  • Running the folder, with shiny::runApp("myapp"), RStudio’s Run App button, Shiny Server or Posit Connect: Shiny loads R/, then runs app.R with the folder as the working directory. root is the app’s folder, and everything above works.
  • Running the app object, by printing what app.R returns (at the console, sourcing it with echo, or Rscript app.R): Shiny does neither. The paths are relative to wherever R happens to be, and R/ is not loaded, so cars does not exist and app.R stops with an error. Run the folder instead: Rscript -e 'shiny::runApp("myapp")'.

root can be set to an absolute path, for an app whose files live somewhere other than the working directory. That does not load R/; only running the folder does.
